title: The test fixtures under data/ are reviewed: what each is for, what is dead, and how one is rebuilt
body:
The test data under `data/` at 56db6ff: 11 FASTA inputs and 4 `.sufr` copies in `data/inputs/`, 16 `.sufr` files and 9 `.out` files in `data/expected/`, 1.8 MB in all. Ken made them in 2024 for the tests of the day; the scripts that rebuilt them, `mk_test_files.py` and the Makefile, were deleted in 56db6ff because nothing ran them and one would have rebuilt the fixtures wrong. This issue reviews what is there and decides what stays.

What the inventory on 2026-11-03 found:

- Dead files. `1d.sufr` is format version 4 and cannot be opened; `1m.sufr` fails to open with "Bytes must be 1 or 0"; `1s.sufr`, `locate2.out` and `data/inputs/abba.sufr` are read by no test.
- Copies. `data/inputs/{1,2,3,abba}.sufr` are byte-identical to the `data/expected/` files of the same name. Tests read `inputs/1.sufr` fourteen times and `inputs/2.sufr` and `3.sufr` once each.
- Names. `1`, `2`, `3`, `1n`, `2ns`, `2d` say nothing about what the input exercises. `1.fa` is `ACGTNnacgt`, one record with an N and lowercase; `2.fa` is two records with lowercase; `3.fa` has a run of ten N; `abba.fa` is a non-DNA text; `mostlya1`, `mostlya2` and `spaced_input` serve the seed-mask tests; `smol.fa` is three short DNA records; `uniprot.fa` is 296 protein records; `long_dna_sequence.fa` has a run of 2000 N.
- Provenance. Every `.sufr` in `data/expected/` is the tool's own output, committed by Ken; the current code reproduces 13 of them byte for byte through `create_bytes_match_fixtures`. Every `.out` file came from running the binary, per the comments in `sufr/tests/cli.rs`. The oracle in `libsufr/tests/oracle.rs` and the hand-derived tests in `libsufr/tests/search.rs` are the only expectations not produced by the code under test.
- No way to rebuild. With the scripts gone, the flags each fixture was built with live only in `create_bytes_match_fixtures`.

## Proposal

Decide for each file whether a test needs it, delete the rest, and give what stays a name that says what it is for. Record the build flags of every `.sufr` fixture in one place, the bytes test, so a fixture can be regenerated on purpose when the format or the sort changes.

## Open

- Whether the `.out` files stay, or their tests move to hand-derived expectations like `libsufr/tests/search.rs`.
- Whether `uniprot.fa` and `long_dna_sequence.fa`, the two real-sized inputs, are the right ones to keep as regression fixtures.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/4a93ac40
notes.text:
Inventory at feaa5e8, after 3944856 removed `-a`, and a proposal. Jack has put this on hold for a review with Jeb, since it renames fixtures from dev.

## What is there

| group | files | used by |
|---|---|---|
| FASTA inputs | 11 in `data/inputs/` | all, by the oracle, the CLI tests, the search tests and the mask tests in `libsufr/src/lib.rs` |
| `.sufr` fixtures | 13 in `data/expected/` | 12 checked byte for byte by `create_bytes_match_fixtures` in `sufr/tests/cli.rs` |
| `.out` files | 9 in `data/expected/` | 8 compared with CLI output |
| `.sufr` copies | 4 in `data/inputs/` | `1.sufr` read about 15 times as a ready-made file, `2` and `3` once each |

The case list of `create_bytes_match_fixtures` is the one record of how each `.sufr` fixture is built: name, input and flags.

## Proposal

A. Delete the dead files. `data/expected/1s.sufr` and `data/expected/locate2.out` are read by no test. `data/inputs/abba.sufr` is read by no test and is stale: its header byte 2 is still 0.

B. Delete `data/inputs/{1,2,3}.sufr`. Each is byte-identical to the file of the same name in `data/expected/`, and the 20 or so references would point there. Two copies drift, as `abba.sufr` did.

C. Rename the fixtures whose names are now wrong. Each is a name from dev, so Jeb should agree.

| now | proposed | why |
|---|---|---|
| `1n.sufr` | `1-bytes.sufr` | "n" meant N allowed; it is now a build without `--dna` |
| `2n.sufr` | `2-bytes.sufr` | the same |
| `long_dna_sequence_allow_ambiguity.sufr` | `long_dna_sequence-bytes.sufr` | `-a` is gone |
| `2d.sufr` | `2-delimiter-N.sufr` | built with `--sequence-delimiter N` |
| `2s.sufr` | `2-softmask.sufr` | built with `--ignore-softmask` |

The input names (`1.fa`, `2.fa` and the rest) stay, since the tests use them throughout. Item D describes them instead.

D. A way to rebuild. An environment variable such as `SUFR_REGENERATE=1` makes `create_bytes_match_fixtures` write its output over each fixture in place of comparing, so the flags stay in one place and a rebuild is one deliberate command. A short `data/README.md` gives one line per input on what it exercises, and that command.

E. Left as they are. The `.out` files stay, since they pin the CLI's output. Whether they move to hand-derived expectations is a later question. `uniprot.fa` and `long_dna_sequence.fa` stay as the two real-sized inputs.
